title: The design system has the pieces the video mocks are made of
goal: The video mocks are built from pieces the app's shared design library does not have yet (a transport, clip bars, track headers, a time ruler, a playhead, a picker of thumbnail tiles, keyframe marks), so every video feature drew its own. Add them to the shared library once, matching the mocks, so the timeline and everything after it use the same ones.
notes:
Intake detail (the goal as first filed, moved here by triage 2026-09-23): The video mocks use components the SwiftUI design system does not have, so each task drew its own. Target: the user's mocks (docs/design/mocks/pages/video.html, video-shell.html, comp-video.html and the page named here) at their fidelity; runner-prompt rules on default config, side-by-side with the mock, labels-not-explanations and right-click apply. Ask throughout: would a Premiere editor get this, and is it easier here?

Filed from the 2026-09-23 video audit in the intake window.
acceptance: Inventory the mock components (transport, clip bar, track header, ruler, playhead, tile popover, dropdown row, keyframe diamond) against Sources/Photonz shared components
Each missing one becomes a shared SwiftUI component with its tokens from inspector.css/overlays.css and an ImageRenderer snapshot next to the mock

log.note: triage 2026-09-23: goal rewritten in plain language, the old one kept at the top of notes; depends on the-video-mocks-are-the-user-s-again-and-d18-is

video-shell.html was deleted on 2026-09-23 (task the-video-mocks-are-the-user-s-again-and-d18-is): it was the loop's own study arguing against tracks. The target is now pages/video.html, the video-*.html walkthroughs and comp-video.html, restored as the user drew them, plus UX-PATTERNS D18 (rewritten: a document with time has tracks). Where this task mentions video-shell, read video.html.

Inventory (mock piece -> what the app has): TRANSPORT (overlays.css .transport/.scrub) -> DocumentTransportBar is glyph buttons + timecodes, no scrubber, no volume, no primary round play; PlaybackScrubber is the old QuickTime-neutral bar (white fill, no marks). Missing. CLIP BAR (.clip + video.css .lbl/.speed/.edge/.kfm/.wave) -> MotionStripBar is a private accent-gradient timing bar; ClipPiecesBar draws recording pieces. Missing. TRACK HEADER (.track .tl) -> nothing; MotionStrip draws layer hairlines. Missing. RULER (.ruler) -> MotionStripRulerView, private, ms ticks, 15pt. Partial. PLAYHEAD (.playhead, red, triangle head) -> DocumentPlayheadView is private, accent circle + 1.5pt line. Missing. TILE PICKER (.libgrid/.libtile, .libtile.tt transition thumbs) -> LibraryTile is private to LibraryPanel; transitions picked from a radio list. Missing. DROPDOWN ROW (.irow + .select) -> SelectionMenu is caption-above + native pop-up, not the 76pt label column + raised select face. Missing. KEY DIAMOND (.kfkey) -> KeyDiamondButton, private to PropertyKeysInspector. Exists, not shared. Also TRANSITION BAND (.xband) -> nothing.

Adversarial review before building: (1) the risk is building a second, unused library while the timeline task draws its own again, so every piece is a plain value-in/closure-out SwiftUI view with no EditorState, which is what lets the-timeline-is-the-one-in-the-mock assemble them directly. (2) A snapshot of a copy proves nothing, so the gallery script compiles the SHIPPED kit files with swiftc and renders them; the kit must stay free of app types for that to work, and the script failing to compile is the guard. (3) Menus are AppKit-backed and ImageRenderer cannot draw them, so the dropdown row is split into a face (drawn) and a Menu wrapper. (4) Accent: the app maps --accent to the system accent everywhere, so the kit does too; every other token is the mock's hex, light and dark. (5) video.html's timeline overrides the shared track header (84pt, not uppercase) while inspector.css is 58pt uppercase; the header takes both as parameters rather than picking one.

Built: Sources/Photonz/VideoKit (VideoKit.swift tokens+metrics, VideoKitTransport, VideoKitTimeline, VideoKitPicker, VideoKitControls), Sources/Photonz/VideoKitHover.swift (the kitHover seam -> playtestHover, forced by PlaytestHoverIsReachableTests). Snapshots: Scripts/video-kit-gallery.sh compiles ONLY the kit + gallery with swiftc and ImageRenders each piece into docs/design/mocks/shared/video-kit/kit-*.png; index.html there draws the same data with the mock's CSS beside each render (side-by-side.png). Differences found and fixed on the comparison: key diamond 8->11pt (mock's .kfkey is content-box + 1.5px border), push thumbnail widened its tile (now a Canvas), automatic track header keeps its case. Remaining deliberate difference: system accent instead of --accent. Scripts/test.sh now typechecks the kit alone. Migrated: the Animating section's KeyDiamondButton draws VideoKit.KeyDiamond; key-a-title-s-scale-walk passes at default config (no flags) with 8 real captures. UX-PATTERNS D18 gained 'The video kit' table (mock class -> kit piece).

left rough (not filed): SF Symbols stand in for the mock's icon set (skip, volume, track kinds); the rest of the app's icons are SF Symbols too, so this is the house choice rather than a defect. Accent choice is an evaluate question in the audit for the user to react to. Test run 1 also hit the export-size budget flake, already owned by the-export-size-test-fails-about-one-run-in-thre; run 2 was fully green.

Shared video kit in Sources/Photonz/VideoKit (transport, scrubber, track row/header, ruler, playhead, clip bar with key marks/speed/grips/waveform, transition band, picker tiles/grid/transition thumbnails, key diamond, field row, dropdown) on the mock's tokens. Each piece rendered by ImageRenderer from the shipped source (Scripts/video-kit-gallery.sh) beside the mock's own CSS at /shared/video-kit/index.html; UX-PATTERNS D18 lists them. Animating section's diamond now uses the kit; key-a-title-s-scale-walk green at default config; Scripts/test.sh green (9251 tests + kit-alone typecheck). Audit queue/audits/2026-09-23-video-kit.json.
